scenario.title: Support backlog
scenario.initial_request: Build a chatbot so customers stop waiting for answers about refunds

M-IBAN-FAILURE-RATE.name: Rate of refund execution failures due to invalid IBAN format
M-IBAN-FAILURE-RATE.denominator: total refund execution attempts recorded in payment-db

M-TICKET-MEDIAN-RESPONSE-TIME.name: Median first-response time for support tickets

M-REFUND-FAILURE-TICKET-SHARE.name: Share of open refund-related tickets attributable to IBAN-format refund failures
M-REFUND-FAILURE-TICKET-SHARE.numerator: tickets linked to a refund_failures record with status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT
M-REFUND-FAILURE-TICKET-SHARE.denominator: total open refund-related tickets in ticket-db

F-01.statement: All 5 refund_failures records retrieved from payment-db have status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT.

F-02.statement: ticket-db response_times reports median_hours=2.0, sla_hours=24.0, tickets=900 for the sampled period.

CL-01.statement: Build a chatbot so customers stop waiting for answers about refunds

CL-02.statement: Customers wait forever; a chatbot would answer instantly.

H-NO-SELF-SERVICE-CHANNEL.statement: Customers wait because there is no self-service way to get answers about refund status/policy; a chatbot answering common questions would resolve the backlog.

H-PAYMENT-PROCESSING-DELAY.statement: Customers are actually waiting for the refund payment itself to be processed (not for an answer), so tickets pile up because the underlying DA-PAY refund execution is slow.

H-SUPPORT-CAPACITY-SHORTAGE.statement: The backlog stems from insufficient support staffing/triage capacity relative to ticket volume, not from customers lacking an information channel.

H-PROCESS-MISROUTING.statement: Refund tickets already contain or could get a correct answer but are delayed by inefficient routing/handoffs within process P-REF, not by an information gap.

H-TICKET-CONTENT-MISMATCH.statement: The actual customer pain is confusion over refund policy/eligibility (needing judgment), which a scripted chatbot cannot resolve, so the backlog's cause differs from SH-SUP's speed-only framing.

H-IBAN-FORMAT-DATA-QUALITY.statement: Refunds fail at execution due to invalid/incorrectly formatted IBAN data in DA-PAY, generating support tickets as customers follow up on failed refunds rather than lacking information.

interpretation_history.interpretation: All 5 sampled refund_failures records fail with status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT, indicating refunds are blocked by a payment-data validation problem (bad IBAN format) rather than merely delayed or awaiting an informational answer.

Ticket-db shows a median first-response time of 2.0 hours against a 24-hour SLA across 900 tickets, indicating support is responding to tickets quickly rather than leaving customers waiting for an initial answer. This weighs against speed/capacity/routing-based explanations of the "backlog" and is more consistent with tickets persisting because underlying refund execution issues (not response delay) remain unresolved.

E-03.content: Customers wait forever; a chatbot would answer instantly.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-SUP restates their original speed-framed claim (customers "wait forever", a chatbot would answer "instantly"), matching CL-01 which is already recorded as CONTRADICTED by E-01/E-02; this interview adds no new authoritative evidence and instead illustrates SH-SUP's noted bias toward framing the problem as response speed.

U-FAILURE-SCOPE.question: What proportion of the full refund-related ticket backlog is caused by IBAN-format validation failures versus other causes?
U-FAILURE-SCOPE.decision_impact: Determines whether IBAN data-quality remediation alone resolves the backlog or whether other causes must also be addressed.
U-FAILURE-SCOPE.resolution_path: Query the full payment-db refund_failures table and join with ticket-db to measure the actual share, instead of relying on the 5-record sample.
U-FAILURE-SCOPE.safe_placeholder: Proceed with IBAN data-quality investigation as the primary workstream while treating other causes as out of scope until measured.

U-IBAN-ERROR-SOURCE.question: Is the invalid IBAN data caused by customer input error, an upstream data-entry defect, or a validation bug in the refund process P-REF?
U-IBAN-ERROR-SOURCE.decision_impact: Determines whether the eventual fix targets customer-facing input validation, an upstream data pipeline, or refund process logic.
U-IBAN-ERROR-SOURCE.resolution_path: Trace a sample of FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT refunds back through P-REF's intake step to find where invalid data was accepted.
U-IBAN-ERROR-SOURCE.safe_placeholder: Limit activity to read-only investigation of DA-PAY/P-REF; do not change refund execution logic until the source is confirmed.

U-POLICY-CONFUSION-SUBSET.question: Does a distinct subset of tickets reflect genuine refund-policy confusion (H-TICKET-CONTENT-MISMATCH) rather than IBAN execution failures?
U-POLICY-CONFUSION-SUBSET.decision_impact: If present, this subset would not be resolved by IBAN remediation and may need a separate fix outside this problem's scope.
U-POLICY-CONFUSION-SUBSET.resolution_path: Classify ticket content for a sample of tickets not linked to any FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT refund record.
U-POLICY-CONFUSION-SUBSET.safe_placeholder: Treat policy-confusion tickets as out of scope for this remediation until a distinct subset is confirmed by evidence.

A-SAMPLE-REPRESENTATIVE.statement: The 5 sampled refund_failures records are representative of the broader population of refund failures driving the backlog, not an unrepresentative subset.

A-TICKETS-OVERLAP-REFUNDS.statement: The 900 tickets measured in E-02 substantially include the refund-related tickets that make up the backlog SH-SUP describes.

SC-ROOT-CAUSE-CONFIRMED.statement: Confirm across the full refund_failures population (not just the sampled 5) that IBAN-format validation failures are the dominant cause of refund-related tickets.
SC-ROOT-CAUSE-CONFIRMED.threshold: FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT remains the majority status across the full population, consistent with the 5/5 sample
SC-ROOT-CAUSE-CONFIRMED.validation_method: Query the complete payment-db refund_failures table and join with ticket-db instead of relying on the 5-record sample.

SC-REDUCE-IBAN-FAILURES.statement: Reduce the IBAN-format refund execution failure rate after remediating the underlying data-quality issue.
SC-REDUCE-IBAN-FAILURES.threshold: lower than the current sampled 100% (5/5) FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT rate
SC-REDUCE-IBAN-FAILURES.validation_method: Re-run the payment-db refund_failures query after remediation and compare the failure status distribution.

VOB-U-FAILURE-SCOPE.unresolved_question: What proportion of the full refund-related ticket backlog is caused by IBAN-format validation failures versus other causes?
VOB-U-FAILURE-SCOPE.reason_deferred: deferred at DEFINE Gate; safe placeholder: Proceed with IBAN data-quality investigation as the primary workstream while treating other causes as out of scope until measured.
VOB-U-FAILURE-SCOPE.validation_method: Query the full payment-db refund_failures table and join with ticket-db to measure the actual share, instead of relying on the 5-record sample.

VOB-U-IBAN-ERROR-SOURCE.unresolved_question: Is the invalid IBAN data caused by customer input error, an upstream data-entry defect, or a validation bug in the refund process P-REF?
VOB-U-IBAN-ERROR-SOURCE.reason_deferred: deferred at DEFINE Gate; safe placeholder: Limit activity to read-only investigation of DA-PAY/P-REF; do not change refund execution logic until the source is confirmed.
VOB-U-IBAN-ERROR-SOURCE.validation_method: Trace a sample of FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT refunds back through P-REF's intake step to find where invalid data was accepted.

problem_definition.requested_solution: SH-SUP requested building a chatbot so customers "stop waiting" and get instant answers about refunds, framing the backlog as a self-service information gap.
symptoms: Support ticket backlog about refunds reported by SH-SUP (CL-01, CL-02)
All 5 sampled payment-db refund_failures records show status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT (E-01)
Ticket-db median first-response time is 2.0 hours against a 24-hour SLA across 900 tickets, i.e. responses are already fast (E-02)
problem_definition.root_problem: Refund-related support tickets persist as a backlog because refund payments fail at execution due to invalid/incorrectly formatted IBAN data in DA-PAY, causing customers to repeatedly follow up on unresolved failed refunds; this is not caused by slow support response times or a lack of self-service information (E-01, E-02).

decision_log.rationale: causal chain: Refund execution attempts against DA-PAY fail due to invalid/incorrectly formatted IBAN data (E-01: 5/5 sampled refund_failures = FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT). → Customers whose refunds fail follow up repeatedly via support tickets about the unresolved refund (E-01 interpretation). → Tickets accumulate into a visible backlog despite support already responding quickly (E-02: median 2.0h vs 24h SLA across 900 tickets), ruling out slow response as the driver. → The persisting backlog is therefore a refund-execution data-quality problem rather than an information/self-service gap, contrary to SH-SUP's chatbot framing (CL-01/CL-02/E-03).; rejected framings: [('H-NO-SELF-SERVICE-CHANNEL', 'Contradicted by E-01 (refunds fail at execution, not from an information gap) and E-02 (fast median response time shows customers are not stuck waiting for an answer); it only matches the already-contradicted CL-01 and unverified CL-02 stakeholder framing.'), ('H-SUPPORT-CAPACITY-SHORTAGE', "Contradicted by E-02's fast median response time (2.0h vs 24h SLA across 900 tickets), which is inconsistent with a staffing/capacity shortfall."), ('H-PROCESS-MISROUTING', 'Contradicted by E-02; fast first-response times are inconsistent with tickets being stuck in inefficient internal routing.')]
[CONDITIONAL] critical unknown U-FAILURE-SCOPE deferred to VOB-U-FAILURE-SCOPE; [CONDITIONAL] critical unknown U-IBAN-ERROR-SOURCE deferred to VOB-U-IBAN-ERROR-SOURCE

framing_assertion.rationale: The initial_request assumes a chatbot will stop customers waiting for refund answers, i.e. that the bottleneck is absence of an instant-answer channel, framed by SH-SUP whose potential_bias is noted as 'frames everything as response speed'.

hypotheses.statement: Customers wait because there is no self-service way to get answers about refund status/policy; a chatbot answering common questions would resolve the backlog.
hypotheses.rationale: This is SH-SUP's own framing in initial_request and matches the proposed solution; if true, a chatbot is the right fix, but SH-SUP's noted bias ('frames everything as response speed') means it needs independent corroboration.
discriminating_evidence: ticket-db: ticket topics/content showing repetitive, simple, answerable refund-status questions
ticket-db: response times correlated with ticket volume vs. with answer complexity

hypotheses.statement: Customers are actually waiting for the refund payment itself to be processed (not for an answer), so tickets pile up because the underlying DA-PAY refund execution is slow.
hypotheses.rationale: If the true wait is for money movement rather than information, a chatbot only reroutes the complaint and does not fix the backlog; the fix would target payment-db/process P-REF processing speed instead.
discriminating_evidence: payment-db (DA-PAY): refund payment processing/settlement timestamps vs. ticket creation timestamps
ticket-db: whether ticket resolution time tracks payment completion rather than agent response

hypotheses.statement: The backlog stems from insufficient support staffing/triage capacity relative to ticket volume, not from customers lacking an information channel.
hypotheses.rationale: If volume simply exceeds handling capacity, a chatbot may only shift load rather than remove it; the fix would be staffing or triage process changes rather than an automated Q&A tool.
discriminating_evidence: ticket-db: ticket volume trend vs. response-time trend (queueing signature)
ticket-db: whether delays occur before any agent engagement (queue wait) vs. during resolution

hypotheses.statement: Refund tickets already contain or could get a correct answer but are delayed by inefficient routing/handoffs within process P-REF, not by an information gap.
hypotheses.rationale: If delay is procedural (handoff friction within P-REF), a chatbot would not address the structural bottleneck; the fix would be process redesign of P-REF steps/handoffs.
discriminating_evidence: process P-REF: steps/handoffs data once populated, showing where tickets stall
ticket-db: time elapsed per handoff stage versus total resolution time

hypotheses.statement: The actual customer pain is confusion over refund policy/eligibility (needing judgment), which a scripted chatbot cannot resolve, so the backlog's cause differs from SH-SUP's speed-only framing.
hypotheses.rationale: SH-SUP's documented bias toward framing issues as response speed could mask a content/complexity-driven cause; this would require a different solution (clearer policy, better escalation) rather than a chatbot.
discriminating_evidence: ticket-db: categorization of ticket content (status inquiry vs. policy dispute vs. exception handling)
ticket-db: repeat-contact rate per ticket indicating unresolved ambiguity rather than slow first response

actions.question: What is the current rate and pattern of refund payment failures/delays in DA-PAY, and how does it correlate with ticket backlog timing?
actions.expected_information_gain: Directly tests whether the backlog is driven by slow/failing refund execution rather than a missing information channel; this is the exact mechanism H-PAYMENT-PROCESSING-DELAY claims.
actions.decision_impact_rationale: H-PAYMENT-PROCESSING-DELAY is flagged CRITICAL impact; if confirmed, a chatbot would not fix the root cause and the next decision (build chatbot vs fix payment pipeline) flips entirely.
resolves_unknowns: DA-PAY completeness/authority on refund execution timing
actions.why_now: No other catalog item names the refund-payment mechanism this precisely, and the hypothesis it tests has the highest declared decision_impact (CRITICAL) among all live hypotheses.

actions.question: What do ticket volumes, response-time distributions, and handoff/reopen patterns in DA-TCK show about where delay accumulates in P-REF?
actions.expected_information_gain: Separates whether delay comes from lack of a self-service answer channel, from staffing/triage capacity shortage, or from inefficient routing inside P-REF, by showing where time is actually spent.
actions.decision_impact_rationale: Three HIGH/MEDIUM-impact hypotheses (self-service gap, capacity shortage, misrouting) all make distinct predictions about response-time patterns, so this result changes which of three competing fixes is pursued next.
actions.why_now: This is the only catalog item describing ticket timing data, and it is the most direct available test for three still-live, non-rejected hypotheses about where backlog time is lost.

actions.question: Beyond response speed, what specifically do customers ask about in refund tickets — status lookups, policy/eligibility judgment calls, or something else — and does SH-SUP have evidence beyond the initial framing?
actions.expected_information_gain: Probes H-TICKET-CONTENT-MISMATCH (whether tickets need judgment a chatbot can't give) using the only source that can describe ticket content qualitatively, while explicitly accounting for SH-SUP's noted bias toward a speed-only framing.
actions.decision_impact_rationale: If SH-SUP's own account reveals judgment-dependent refund questions, it undercuts the chatbot proposal even on its own framing, which would change the recommended next action.
resolves_unknowns: CL-01 assertion basis (lack_of_self_service_answers) is currently UNVERIFIED
actions.why_now: CL-01 is the stakeholder's unverified initial claim and the only remaining catalog item is a re-interview of its source; it is the last avenue to test the content-mismatch hypothesis given no other data asset describes ticket content.

proposal.stop_reason: All three catalog items (ticket-db:response_times, payment-db:refund_failures, interview:SH-SUP) have been matched to the live hypothesis each most directly tests, with payment-db:refund_failures mapped to H-PAYMENT-PROCESSING-DELAY (its exact mechanism), ticket-db:response_times to the capacity/misrouting/self-service trio, and interview:SH-SUP to H-TICKET-CONTENT-MISMATCH; no catalog item remains unassigned.

proposal.root_problem: Refund-related support tickets persist as a backlog because refund payments fail at execution due to invalid/incorrectly formatted IBAN data in DA-PAY, causing customers to repeatedly follow up on unresolved failed refunds; this is not caused by slow support response times or a lack of self-service information (E-01, E-02).
proposal.requested_solution: SH-SUP requested building a chatbot so customers "stop waiting" and get instant answers about refunds, framing the backlog as a self-service information gap.
symptoms: Support ticket backlog about refunds reported by SH-SUP (CL-01, CL-02)
All 5 sampled payment-db refund_failures records show status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT (E-01)
Ticket-db median first-response time is 2.0 hours against a 24-hour SLA across 900 tickets, i.e. responses are already fast (E-02)
causal_chain: Refund execution attempts against DA-PAY fail due to invalid/incorrectly formatted IBAN data (E-01: 5/5 sampled refund_failures = FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT).
Customers whose refunds fail follow up repeatedly via support tickets about the unresolved refund (E-01 interpretation).
Tickets accumulate into a visible backlog despite support already responding quickly (E-02: median 2.0h vs 24h SLA across 900 tickets), ruling out slow response as the driver.
The persisting backlog is therefore a refund-execution data-quality problem rather than an information/self-service gap, contrary to SH-SUP's chatbot framing (CL-01/CL-02/E-03).

assumptions.statement: The 5 sampled refund_failures records are representative of the broader population of refund failures driving the backlog, not an unrepresentative subset.
The 900 tickets measured in E-02 substantially include the refund-related tickets that make up the backlog SH-SUP describes.

proposal.summary: SH-SUP requested a chatbot framing the backlog as customers lacking self-service refund answers (CL-01, CL-02). Investigation found this framing wrong: payment-db shows all 5 sampled refund_failures records fail with status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT (E-01); ticket-db shows median first-response 2.0h vs 24h SLA across 900 tickets (E-02), so support is already fast. The established root problem (PD-1) is that refund tickets persist because refunds fail at execution due to invalid/incorrectly formatted IBAN data in DA-PAY, not slow support or missing self-service info. The DEFINE gate reached only CONDITIONAL_PASS because two critical unknowns were deferred to open VOBs. Only the narrow correlate_tickets_with_failed_refunds (DA-TCK) scope was released, decision RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION; quantifying the full IBAN-failure scope and remediating the underlying data are excluded, their VOBs still open.
key_points: Problem as defined (PD-1): refund tickets backlog because refunds fail at execution due to invalid/incorrectly formatted IBAN data in DA-PAY (E-01), not slow support or missing self-service info.
SH-SUP's chatbot request (CL-01/CL-02) framed the issue as a self-service information gap; H-NO-SELF-SERVICE-CHANNEL is REJECTED, contradicted by E-01 and E-02.
E-01: 5/5 sampled payment-db refund_failures records show status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT, supporting H-IBAN-FORMAT-DATA-QUALITY (SUPPORTED, CRITICAL impact).
E-02: ticket-db shows median first-response 2.0h vs 24h SLA across 900 tickets, showing response speed is not the backlog driver (rejects H-SUPPORT-CAPACITY-SHORTAGE, H-NO-SELF-SERVICE-CHANNEL).
Released scope is limited to correlate_tickets_with_failed_refunds against DA-TCK (per SD-1 release_scope / minimum_useful_scope); the only work item delivered.
Decision RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, not a hold, because the DEFINE gate was CONDITIONAL_PASS with deferred items tracked as open VOBs rather than a blocking failure.
quantify_iban_failure_scope and remediate_iban_validation_data are excluded because blocked by open VOBs (VOB-U-FAILURE-SCOPE, VOB-U-IBAN-ERROR-SOURCE) required_before BEFORE_RELEASE.
SR-FAILED-REFUND-RECOLLECTION-H (a proposed P-REF re-collection handoff) is only a bridge candidate, not released, since outside PD-1's intended_scope.
limitations_explained: VOB-U-FAILURE-SCOPE is open: the share of the full ticket backlog caused by IBAN-format failures vs other causes beyond the 5-record sample is unknown, so quantify_iban_failure_scope was excluded.

VOB-U-IBAN-ERROR-SOURCE is open: whether invalid IBAN data stems from customer error, an upstream defect, or a P-REF validation bug is unresolved, and the tool surface lacks deploy capability, so remediate_iban_validation_data cannot ship now.
